pharm: Class I (super-potent) topical glucocorticoid with anti-inflammatory, antipruritic and vasoconstrictive activity
quick: Apply a thin layer twice daily; max 50 g/week, up to 2 weeks
Use only if benefit justifies risk; limit amount, area and duration
Caution; do not apply to breast/nipple before nursing
Signs of HPA-axis suppression; local skin atrophy
summary: Clobetasol propionate is a super-high-potency (Class I) topical corticosteroid for short-term relief of inflammatory and pruritic corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses. Because of its potency, treatment is limited to 2 consecutive weeks and 50 g/week to minimise hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression.
indications: Relief of inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses (e.g. plaque psoriasis, eczema, lichen planus)

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer twice daily and rub in gently
dosage.n: Total dose must not exceed 50 g/week
Higher ratio of skin surface to body mass increases systemic risk

admin: Apply a thin layer to affected skin twice daily and rub in gently and completely
Do not use with occlusive dressings
Reassess diagnosis if no improvement within 2 weeks
Avoid face, axillae and groin unless directed
moa: Topical corticosteroids act via binding to intracellular glucocorticoid receptors, inducing anti-inflammatory proteins (e.g. lipocortins) that inhibit phospholipase A2, thereby reducing prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis; they also produce vasoconstriction, antiproliferative and immunosuppressive effects in skin.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to clobetasol propionate or any component
relative: Use on face, groin or axillae
Application to large surface areas or under occlusion

preg: No adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Corticosteroids are teratogenic in animals. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; use the smallest amount, over the smallest area, for the shortest time.
lact: Systemically administered corticosteroids appear in human milk. It is not known whether topical application results in sufficient systemic absorption to be detectable in milk. Use caution; do not apply to the breast/nipple before nursing.
renal: No specific dose adjustment; systemic absorption is generally low with appropriate topical use.

minor: Concomitant potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may theoretically increase systemic corticosteroid exposure with extensive use
interactions.diagnostics: ACTH stimulation test may be used to evaluate suspected HPA-axis suppression

common: Burning, stinging, itching at application site
serious: Cushing syndrome, hyperglycaemia (with extensive systemic absorption)
rare: Folliculitis, hypertrichosis, perioral dermatitis, secondary infection
emergency: Adrenal insufficiency on abrupt withdrawal after suppression

monitoring: Periodic assessment of HPA-axis suppression with prolonged or extensive use
counsel: Apply a thin layer only to affected areas twice daily
Do not exceed 2 weeks or 50 g per week
Do not cover with airtight/occlusive dressings unless directed
Avoid the face, underarms and groin unless told otherwise
Wash hands after application; do not apply to broken/infected skin
pk: Anti-inflammatory effect within hours to days
Systemic absorption variable; minimal with correct use
Store at controlled room temperature; do not freeze
pearls: Class I super-potent steroid - reserve for thick, resistant lesions
Strict 2-week, 50 g/week ceiling to avoid HPA-axis suppression
Avoid abrupt discontinuation after prolonged use; consider step-down to a milder steroid
Not for under-12s or facial/intertriginous skin
missed: Apply the missed dose when remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose; do not apply extra to make up.
overdose: Topical overuse can be absorbed in sufficient amounts to produce systemic corticosteroid effects (HPA-axis suppression, Cushingoid features, hyperglycaemia). Discontinue gradually and treat systemic effects as indicated.
